findings.issue_text: [BUG] MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now declared as `class MetricAlertDetectorHandler(StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]): pass`, but StatefulDetectorHandler defines @abc.abstractmethod methods (get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and the newly added build_occurrence_and_event_data) that this subclass implements with a bare `pass`, so instantiating it raises TypeError('Can't instantiate abstract class ... with abstract methods ...'). Any Detector whose type slug resolves to this group type will crash process_detectors with a TypeError at `detector_handler(detector)` instead of evaluating; previously the class only needed to implement evaluate(), which it did, so this diff converts a working registration into an un-instantiable handler.

[BUG] MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing the newly-added abstract method build_occurrence_and_event_data (or get_dedupe_value / get_group_key_values), so any code that instantiates it raises TypeError("Can't instantiate abstract class"). A detector whose type slug maps to MetricAlertDetectorHandler crashes in Detector.detector_handler -> StatefulDetectorHandler.__init__ as soon as anything constructs the handler (process_detectors currently guards on group_type but any future instantiation site in this PR's design fails hard instead of the intended no-op TODO behavior), blocking the metric-alert detector path entirely.

[ADVISORY] The new occurrence-generation branch has no coverage for transitions between two non-OK priorities (e.g. HIGH -> MEDIUM): no test in tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py exercises evaluate_group_key_value when the status changes while is_active stays True, so the behavior 'active-to-active priority change emits a new IssueOccurrence rather than nothing or a status-change' is unverified. If that path is wrong (e.g. it should emit nothing because the issue is already open), a future regression or the current behavior silently creates duplicate occurrences for every priority flip; nobody notices because no spec pins the expected result for this transition despite the diff rewriting exactly this branch.

[ADVISORY] PriorityLevel(new_status) conversion in the occurrence path is unverified by any test: the diff's tests only cover new_status == HIGH (whose enum values happen to line up), and no test covers the case where a DetectorPriorityLevel member has no corresponding PriorityLevel, which would raise ValueError inside evaluate_group_key_value. If any gating condition returns a DetectorPriorityLevel that maps to a PriorityLevel with a different value/name, a packet that should fire an alert instead raises and the whole data-packet evaluation for that detector is lost; the diff introduces this conversion with no assertion that the mapping is total.

[ADVISORY] The resolution path through process_detectors (a DetectorEvaluationResult carrying a StatusChangeMessage instead of an IssueOccurrence) lost its end-to-end test when the test rework moved resolution coverage into handler-level evaluate tests only, so process_detectors' call to create_issue_occurrence_from_result with a status change is now untested at the integration level. A regression in create_issue_occurrence_from_result's status-change branch (e.g. passing the wrong PayloadType or dropping the status_change argument to produce_occurrence_to_kafka) would silently stop resolving metric-alert issues and no test in this diff would catch it.

[ADVISORY] In test_state_results_multi_group, the expected occurrence for group_2 is built with value 6 while the data packet carries group_val 10, and build_mock_occurrence_and_event ignores its value parameter entirely, so the test cannot detect if evaluate_group_key_value passes the wrong value into build_occurrence_and_event_data. A regression that feeds the group value (e.g. the metric snapshot number) into evidence/subtitle of the occurrence would pass these tests unchanged; the next developer debugging wrong alert payloads has no failing test to anchor against because the helper discards the one argument that distinguishes the two calls.

[BUG] MetricAlertDetectorHandler inherits StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing the newly-added abstract method build_occurrence_and_event_data, leaving it an uninstantiable abstract class. Any code path that instantiates MetricAlertDetectorHandler for a detector of type 'metric_alert' now raises TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class with abstract method 'build_occurrence_and_event_data', so process_detectors fails for that grouptype; the stated intent of wiring occurrences for stateful detectors is not actually delivered for the only real handler in the diff.

[ADVISORY] test_state_results_multi_group builds occurrence_2 for group_2 with value 6 while the packet declares group_2's value as 10, and build_mock_occurrence_and_event ignores the value argument entirely. The test asserts against hardcoded data that does not depend on the actual group value, so a regression where evaluate_group_key_value passes the wrong value (or no value) into build_occurrence_and_event_data would pass this suite; the next contributor extending the occurrence hook gets no real coverage of value propagation.

[BUG] MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now `pass` subclassing StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing any of the newly-required abstract methods (get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, build_occurrence_and_event_data), so instantiating it raises TypeError. Any Detector whose type slug resolves to this registered group type hits `detector.detector_handler` in process_detectors and crashes with TypeError instead of evaluating, taking down the whole detector-processing batch for that packet; previously the class was concrete with a working (no-op) evaluate.

[ADVISORY] The abstract `build_occurrence_and_event_data` was added to the base DetectorHandler class rather than StatefulDetectorHandler, forcing every detector handler — stateful or not — to implement occurrence construction. The next non-stateful handler author must implement a hook that belongs to the stateful state-machine logic; out-of-tree/in-tree DetectorHandler subclasses that don't implement it fail at instantiation even though occurrence production is meaningless without the state machine. The tests' MockDetectorHandler avoids this only because it is never instantiated as a handler instance.

[ADVISORY] Duplicate group keys are now silently overwritten by the dict-keyed results (`results[result.group_key] = result`), removing the explicit duplicate-detection error log that existed before. If a handler ever emits two distinct results for the same group key (the condition the old code logged as 'shouldn't happen - investigate'), the first occurrence is silently dropped with no error/metric; a handler bug becomes invisible instead of observable.

[ADVISORY] `PriorityLevel(new_status)` performs a raw int-value cast from DetectorPriorityLevel to PriorityLevel with no explicit mapping, assuming both enums share member values. If DetectorPriorityLevel's numeric values drift from PriorityLevel's (e.g. a MEDIUM level added to one and not the other), the occurrence is produced with a wrong or ValueError-crashing priority; the coupling is unexpressed in code and tests only cover HIGH.

[BUG] MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now a bare `pass` subclass of StatefulDetectorHandler, inheriting three abstract methods (get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, build_occurrence_and_event_data) it does not implement, so it is uninstantiable. Detector.detector_handler for any detector with type 'metric_alert' raises TypeError ('Can't instantiate abstract class') when process_detectors dispatches to it, crashing the ingestion path with a 500/exception instead of the previous no-op `return []` behavior this handler deliberately provided.

[BUG] build_occurrence_and_event_data is declared as an abstractmethod on the base DetectorHandler class, forcing every DetectorHandler subclass — not just stateful ones — to implement occurrence-building. Any plain DetectorHandler implementation (e.g. the MockDetectorHandler in tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py, and any out-of-tree handlers) now fails to instantiate with TypeError, even though occurrence generation is a stateful-detector concern.

[ADVISORY] The change from a list to a dict silently replaces the previous explicit duplicate-group-key detection (error log + skip of later results) with last-wins overwriting, and the accompanying test_state_results_multi_group_dupe regression test is deleted. A detector implementation that returns duplicate group keys now has its earlier results silently discarded with no log/metric, so whoever debugs lost occurrences for a group has no signal; the intentional dupes-dropped contract from the prior code is removed without a replacement invariant documented in evaluate().

[ADVISORY] In test_state_results_multi_group, the expected occurrence for group_2 is built with value 6 while the actual evaluation used value 10, and the test still passes because build_mock_occurrence_and_event ignores the value argument. The test asserts an occurrence unrelated to the actual group value, so a future regression where build_occurrence_and_event_data receives the wrong value (e.g. wrong group_key's value under dict iteration) will pass CI while producing occurrences with incorrect evidence/subtitle in production.

[BUG] MetricAlertDetectorHandler now inherits StatefulDetectorHandler, which declares the new abstract method build_occurrence_and_event_data, so instantiating MetricAlertDetectorHandler raises TypeError — and no test anywhere in the diff exercises this class, so the breakage is invisible to the suite. Any detector whose type slug resolves to this registered group type will crash at Detector.detector_handler property instantiation (TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class), and process_detectors will fail for all metric-alert detectors; the checked test files (tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py, tests/sentry/issues/test_grouptype.py via BaseGroupTypeTest) contain zero references to MetricAlertDetectorHandler, so CI stays green while the only real handler is broken.

[BUG] test_state_results_multi_group builds expected occurrence_2 with value 6 even though the packet supplies group_2=10, and the test still passes because build_mock_occurrence_and_event ignores the value parameter entirely — proving the group value plumbed into build_occurrence_and_event_data is never verified by any assertion. If the production evaluate_group_key_value passes the wrong group value (e.g. the dedupe value, or a stale value from a previous iteration) into build_occurrence_and_event_data, every test in this diff stays green and the wrong evidence/value ships in real occurrences; the expectation object is factually wrong for the input and the suite cannot detect it.

[ADVISORY] The expected occurrences in test_state_results, test_state_results_multi_group, TestEvaluate.test, test_above_below_threshold, test_results_on_change, and test_dedupe are constructed by the very same build_mock_occurrence_and_event helper that MockDetectorStateHandler.build_occurrence_and_event_data delegates to, so the occurrence payload assertions are tautological — the test helper is compared against itself, not against independently specified expected content. A regression that mutates the occurrence payload between the hook call and the kafka producer (e.g. in create_issue_occurrence_from_result) would be caught, but any wrong field inside the hook contract — title, evidence, fingerprint inputs, priority mapping PriorityLevel(new_status) — is unverifiable by these tests; the next person changing the hook signature or payload has no spec to test against and will simply update the helper, keeping both wrong together.

[ADVISORY] The resolve path through process_detectors — evaluate_group_key_value returning a StatusChangeMessage that create_issue_occurrence_from_result sends as a PayloadType.STATUS_CHANGE payload — has no test in this diff; only the PayloadType.OCCURRENCE calls are asserted (mocked produce_occurrence_to_kafka is asserted with status_change=None in every test). The diff changed the control flow around result construction in evaluate_group_key_value (result typed StatusChangeMessage | IssueOccurrence and the else-branch added), yet nothing verifies that a group transitioning to OK causes process_detectors to emit a status-change payload with the correct fingerprint/group_id; a regression that drops or mangles the resolve path (e.g. PriorityLevel(new_status) crashing, or create_issue_occurrence_from_result mishandling StatusChangeMessage) is caught by no test, leaving issues unresolvable in production while the suite is green; I checked tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py — test_above_below_threshold only asserts the returned StatusChangeMessage object from evaluate, never its transport through process_detectors.

[ADVISORY] test_results_on_change and test_dedupe in TestEvaluate pass actual values of 100 and 8 in group_vals but construct expected occurrences with value 6, which passes only because the helper ignores the value — the same false-confidence pattern as multi_group, showing the value parameter is dead in the entire expected-vs-actual comparison across the suite. Anyone reading these tests will believe the occurrence reflects the evaluated group value; in reality the parameter is unasserted everywhere, so the next refactor of evaluate's value plumbing has no safety net.

[BUG] MetricAlertDetectorHandler inherits StatefulDetectorHandler's two abstract methods (evaluate and build_occurrence_and_event_data) without implementing either, so instantiating it raises TypeError('Can't instantiate abstract class'). Any detector whose registered grouptype resolves to MetricAlertDetectorHandler crashes at `handler = detector.detector_handler`-style construction inside process_detectors; previously the class instantiated fine and evaluate() returned [], so this diff turns the metric-alert path from a no-op into an unhandled TypeError that aborts processing of the whole data packet for all detectors in the list.

[ADVISORY] The explicit duplicate-group-key guard (logger.error("Duplicate detector state group keys found") plus skip) was replaced by dict insertion `results[result.group_key] = result`, which silently overwrites a duplicate with the later one. If a subclass's get_group_key_values or evaluate path ever yields duplicate group keys (the condition the old code explicitly flagged as 'shouldn't happen - investigate'), the first result's enqueued state updates and Kafka-produced occurrence still execute while the result object is silently replaced with no log, making the invariant violation invisible to operators debugging state divergence.

[ADVISORY] The `result: StatusChangeMessage | IssueOccurrence` local is annotated but the OK branch assigns only a StatusChangeMessage while event_data stays None, and the non-OK branch delegates to a handler-provided build_occurrence_and_event_data with no validation that the returned occurrence's fingerprint/type match the detector's registered grouptype. A concrete handler returning an occurrence whose `type` is None or unregistered (e.g. built from `detector.group_type` when the slug lookup silently returns None) is passed to create_issue_occurrence_from_result and produce_occurrence_to_kafka, failing downstream in the Kafka consumer after the evaluation is already reported as a result — a silent partial success where the worker-side failure surfaces far from the producer code that caused it.

adjudication.rationale: Diff adds new behavior in `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate_group_key_value`: when `new_status != OK`, it now always calls `build_occurrence_and_event_data(...)` and returns an `IssueOccurrence` (vs previously TODO/no occurrence). This will also run for non-OK -> non-OK transitions (e.g. HIGH->MEDIUM) as long as the status changes, even though `is_active` remains True. The updated tests in `tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py` cover inactive->active (emits occurrence) and active->OK (emits `StatusChangeMessage`), but there is no test exercising an active-to-active priority change to pin whether it should emit a new occurrence or not. That’s a specific, diff-grounded missing test for newly introduced nontrivial logic, not a provable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new enum conversion in `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate_group_key_value`: `PriorityLevel(new_status)` is used when building an occurrence (`else: result, event_data = self.build_occurrence_and_event_data(..., PriorityLevel(new_status))`). The updated tests exercise the occurrence path only for `DetectorPriorityLevel.HIGH` (and the OK/resolve path which avoids the conversion), so they do not verify that all possible `DetectorPriorityLevel` values are valid inputs to `PriorityLevel(...)` or that the mapping is total. If any `DetectorPriorityLevel` value lacks a corresponding `PriorityLevel`, this would raise `ValueError` at runtime; while that potential mismatch cannot be confirmed from this diff alone, the missing coverage for this new conversion is a concrete, diff-grounded review issue.

However, the diff alone cannot verify that the enums currently differ, so it's not a proven defect in current behavior.

Detector.detector_handler for any detector with type 'metric_alert' raises TypeError ('Can't instantiate abstract class') when process_detectors dispatches to it, crashing the ingestion path with a 500/exception instead of the previous no-op `return []` behavior this handler deliberately provided.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py`, `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` was changed from a concrete `DetectorHandler` implementation with `evaluate()` returning `[]` to `class MetricAlertDetectorHandler(StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]): pass`. In `src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py`, `StatefulDetectorHandler` is explicitly abstract (it declares abstract `get_group_key_values()` and `build_occurrence_and_event_data()` in this diff, and it already relies on subclass implementations such as `get_dedupe_value()` as shown by the test subclass). Therefore `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` is an abstract class and cannot be instantiated; any code path that resolves this handler via `Detector.detector_handler` and instantiates `group_type.detector_handler(detector)` would raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class ...`, regressing from the prior deliberate no-op behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] build_occurrence_and_event_data is declared as an abstractmethod on the base DetectorHandler class, forcing every DetectorHandler subclass — not just stateful ones — to implement occurrence-building. Any plain DetectorHandler implementation (e.g. the MockDetectorHandler in tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py, and any out-of-tree handlers) now fails to instantiate with TypeError, even though occurrence generation is a stateful-detector concern.

adjudication.rationale: The new abstractmethod `build_occurrence_and_event_data(...)` is added in `StatefulDetectorHandler` (it appears alongside other stateful-only hooks like `get_group_key_values` and is used by `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate_group_key_value`). It is not added to the base `DetectorHandler` abstract class. This is corroborated by the diff updating `MockDetectorHandler` to still subclass `DetectorHandler` without implementing `build_occurrence_and_event_data`, which would fail to instantiate if the finding were true.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The change from a list to a dict silently replaces the previous explicit duplicate-group-key detection (error log + skip of later results) with last-wins overwriting, and the accompanying test_state_results_multi_group_dupe regression test is deleted. A detector implementation that returns duplicate group keys now has its earlier results silently discarded with no log/metric, so whoever debugs lost occurrences for a group has no signal; the intentional dupes-dropped contract from the prior code is removed without a replacement invariant documented in evaluate().

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes explicit duplicate `group_key` detection/logging in `process_detectors` (the `detector_group_keys` set + error log block is deleted) and changes the handler contract from `list[DetectorEvaluationResult]` to `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`. In `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate`, results are now accumulated via `results[result.group_key] = result`, which would last-write-wins if duplicates ever arise during construction, and the prior regression test for dupes (`test_state_results_multi_group_dupe`) is removed. However, with the new dict-based API, duplicates are not representable at the framework boundary, so this is more a removed safety/invariant/diagnostic than a directly verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] In test_state_results_multi_group, the expected occurrence for group_2 is built with value 6 while the actual evaluation used value 10, and the test still passes because build_mock_occurrence_and_event ignores the value argument. The test asserts an occurrence unrelated to the actual group value, so a future regression where build_occurrence_and_event_data receives the wrong value (e.g. wrong group_key's value under dict iteration) will pass CI while producing occurrences with incorrect evidence/subtitle in production.
matched_golden_ids: Wrong value `6` passed for `group_2` occurrence — the data packet specifies `"group_2": 10`. Should be `10` to accurately reflect the test scenario, which will ensure the test produces the correct occurrence data.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same core problem: the test constructs/uses an expected occurrence for group_2 with value 6 even though the packet/evaluation uses 10. It also adds extra context (mock ignoring the value), but the underlying mismatch (should be 10, not 6) matches the golden issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] MetricAlertDetectorHandler now inherits StatefulDetectorHandler, which declares the new abstract method build_occurrence_and_event_data, so instantiating MetricAlertDetectorHandler raises TypeError — and no test anywhere in the diff exercises this class, so the breakage is invisible to the suite. Any detector whose type slug resolves to this registered group type will crash at Detector.detector_handler property instantiation (TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class), and process_detectors will fail for all metric-alert detectors; the checked test files (tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py, tests/sentry/issues/test_grouptype.py via BaseGroupTypeTest) contain zero references to MetricAlertDetectorHandler, so CI stays green while the only real handler is broken.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py`, `StatefulDetectorHandler` now declares a new `@abc.abstractmethod build_occurrence_and_event_data(...)`, and its `evaluate(...)` implementation calls `self.build_occurrence_and_event_data(...)` when `new_status != OK`. In `src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py`, `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` was changed to subclass `StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]` but is now just `pass`, so it does not implement required abstract methods (including `build_occurrence_and_event_data`, and also any other abstract hooks on `StatefulDetectorHandler`). Therefore, if any `GroupType` points `detector_handler = MetricAlertDetectorHandler`, `Detector.detector_handler` will attempt to instantiate it and will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class ...`. The test changes add a mock stateful handler implementing the new abstract method, but nothing in the diff exercises `MetricAlertDetectorHandler`, so this breakage would not be caught by the updated suite.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] test_state_results_multi_group builds expected occurrence_2 with value 6 even though the packet supplies group_2=10, and the test still passes because build_mock_occurrence_and_event ignores the value parameter entirely — proving the group value plumbed into build_occurrence_and_event_data is never verified by any assertion. If the production evaluate_group_key_value passes the wrong group value (e.g. the dedupe value, or a stale value from a previous iteration) into build_occurrence_and_event_data, every test in this diff stays green and the wrong evidence/value ships in real occurrences; the expectation object is factually wrong for the input and the suite cannot detect it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `test_state_results_multi_group` creates `data_packet` with `group_vals` `{ "group_1": 6, "group_2": 10 }` but builds `occurrence_2` via `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(..., "group_2", 6, ...)` (value mismatch). Also, `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` never uses its `value` argument at all (it only uses `group_key`, `new_status`, and handler/detector fields), so the tests cannot verify that `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate_group_key_value` is plumbing the correct `value` into `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. This is a real, diff-grounded test coverage gap/incorrect expected setup, but not a verifiable production defect in the shown code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The expected occurrences in test_state_results, test_state_results_multi_group, TestEvaluate.test, test_above_below_threshold, test_results_on_change, and test_dedupe are constructed by the very same build_mock_occurrence_and_event helper that MockDetectorStateHandler.build_occurrence_and_event_data delegates to, so the occurrence payload assertions are tautological — the test helper is compared against itself, not against independently specified expected content. A regression that mutates the occurrence payload between the hook call and the kafka producer (e.g. in create_issue_occurrence_from_result) would be caught, but any wrong field inside the hook contract — title, evidence, fingerprint inputs, priority mapping PriorityLevel(new_status) — is unverifiable by these tests; the next person changing the hook signature or payload has no spec to test against and will simply update the helper, keeping both wrong together.

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows MockDetectorStateHandler.build_occurrence_and_event_data delegates directly to build_mock_occurrence_and_event (tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py). The same build_mock_occurrence_and_event helper is then used inside test_state_results, test_state_results_multi_group, and multiple TestEvaluate cases to construct the "expected" IssueOccurrence and event_data that are compared against the handler output / kafka producer calls. This makes those assertions largely self-referential: changes to occurrence fields produced by the hook can be mirrored by updating the helper, so the tests don't independently specify/verify hook contract details like title/subtitle, evidence fields, fingerprint composition inputs, or PriorityLevel mapping. This is a specific, diff-grounded test robustness concern, not a runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The resolve path through process_detectors — evaluate_group_key_value returning a StatusChangeMessage that create_issue_occurrence_from_result sends as a PayloadType.STATUS_CHANGE payload — has no test in this diff; only the PayloadType.OCCURRENCE calls are asserted (mocked produce_occurrence_to_kafka is asserted with status_change=None in every test). The diff changed the control flow around result construction in evaluate_group_key_value (result typed StatusChangeMessage | IssueOccurrence and the else-branch added), yet nothing verifies that a group transitioning to OK causes process_detectors to emit a status-change payload with the correct fingerprint/group_id; a regression that drops or mangles the resolve path (e.g. PriorityLevel(new_status) crashing, or create_issue_occurrence_from_result mishandling StatusChangeMessage) is caught by no test, leaving issues unresolvable in production while the suite is green; I checked tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py — test_above_below_threshold only asserts the returned StatusChangeMessage object from evaluate, never its transport through process_detectors.

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `evaluate_group_key_value` now constructs either a `StatusChangeMessage` (OK path) or an `IssueOccurrence` via the new `build_occurrence_and_event_data` (else path), and `process_detectors` now iterates `detector_results.values()` and calls `create_issue_occurrence_from_result` for any non-None `result.result`. The updated tests in `tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py` that mock `produce_occurrence_to_kafka` only assert `PayloadType.OCCURRENCE` with `status_change=None` (e.g. `test_state_results*`). The only OK/resolve assertion is in `TestEvaluate.test_above_below_threshold`, which checks the returned `StatusChangeMessage` from `handler.evaluate(...)` directly, not that `process_detectors(...)`/`create_issue_occurrence_from_result(...)` emits a `PayloadType.STATUS_CHANGE` payload. So the finding about missing transport-level coverage for the resolve path is supported by the diff, but it’s about test coverage rather than a demonstrated defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] test_results_on_change and test_dedupe in TestEvaluate pass actual values of 100 and 8 in group_vals but construct expected occurrences with value 6, which passes only because the helper ignores the value — the same false-confidence pattern as multi_group, showing the value parameter is dead in the entire expected-vs-actual comparison across the suite. Anyone reading these tests will believe the occurrence reflects the evaluated group value; in reality the parameter is unasserted everywhere, so the next refactor of evaluate's value plumbing has no safety net.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows multiple tests in `TestEvaluate` calling `handler.evaluate(... group_vals: {"val1": 100}` and `{...: 8}` but building expected data via `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", 6, PriorityLevel.HIGH)` (e.g. in `test_results_on_change` and `test_dedupe`). The helper `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(...)` accepts `value` but never uses it when constructing the `IssueOccurrence` or `event_data` (it only uses `group_key`, `handler.detector.*`, and timestamps). Therefore the tests cannot detect regressions in plumbing the evaluated `value` into the occurrence/event payload, matching the finding’s claim of false confidence. This is a test-quality gap introduced by the new occurrence-building abstraction, not an immediate product defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] MetricAlertDetectorHandler inherits StatefulDetectorHandler's two abstract methods (evaluate and build_occurrence_and_event_data) without implementing either, so instantiating it raises TypeError('Can't instantiate abstract class'). Any detector whose registered grouptype resolves to MetricAlertDetectorHandler crashes at `handler = detector.detector_handler`-style construction inside process_detectors; previously the class instantiated fine and evaluate() returned [], so this diff turns the metric-alert path from a no-op into an unhandled TypeError that aborts processing of the whole data packet for all detectors in the list.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py`, `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` was changed from a concrete `DetectorHandler` with an implemented `evaluate()` to `class MetricAlertDetectorHandler(StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]): pass`. In `src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py`, `StatefulDetectorHandler` now has the abstract method `build_occurrence_and_event_data(...)` (and still requires `evaluate()` via the abstract base), so a subclass with only `pass` remains abstract and will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class` if constructed. Since `Detector.detector_handler` is used by `process_detectors` to get a handler instance and call `evaluate`, any detector whose `GroupType.detector_handler` points at this class would now crash at construction, whereas previously it was instantiable and returned an empty result list.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The explicit duplicate-group-key guard (logger.error("Duplicate detector state group keys found") plus skip) was replaced by dict insertion `results[result.group_key] = result`, which silently overwrites a duplicate with the later one. If a subclass's get_group_key_values or evaluate path ever yields duplicate group keys (the condition the old code explicitly flagged as 'shouldn't happen - investigate'), the first result's enqueued state updates and Kafka-produced occurrence still execute while the result object is silently replaced with no log, making the invariant violation invisible to operators debugging state divergence.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the handler contract to return a dict keyed by DetectorGroupKey (`evaluate(...) -> dict[...]`) and `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` builds `group_values` as a dict (`get_group_key_values(...) -> dict[str, int]`) then iterates `group_values.items()`, so duplicate group keys cannot occur in this path (a dict cannot contain duplicate keys). The removed duplicate-key guard in `process_detectors` therefore no longer applies to results coming from `StatefulDetectorHandler`, and the specific scenario described (two results with the same key both being evaluated/produced then one being silently overwritten) is not realizable from the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The `result: StatusChangeMessage | IssueOccurrence` local is annotated but the OK branch assigns only a StatusChangeMessage while event_data stays None, and the non-OK branch delegates to a handler-provided build_occurrence_and_event_data with no validation that the returned occurrence's fingerprint/type match the detector's registered grouptype. A concrete handler returning an occurrence whose `type` is None or unregistered (e.g. built from `detector.group_type` when the slug lookup silently returns None) is passed to create_issue_occurrence_from_result and produce_occurrence_to_kafka, failing downstream in the Kafka consumer after the evaluation is already reported as a result — a silent partial success where the worker-side failure surfaces far from the producer code that caused it.

adjudication.rationale: In `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate_group_key_value`, the non-OK path now unconditionally accepts whatever `build_occurrence_and_event_data(...)` returns and forwards it via `DetectorEvaluationResult` to `create_issue_occurrence_from_result` (and tests show this ultimately calls `produce_occurrence_to_kafka`) with no validation of required fields like `IssueOccurrence.type` matching the detector’s registered `GroupType` (`Detector.group_type` can be `None` by contract). The diff doesn’t prove a concrete downstream crash, but it does introduce/solidify an API where a misbehaving handler can emit malformed occurrences without early, local failure or logging. The comment about the OK branch/event_data being None is not itself a defect since `event_data` is allowed to be None in that branch.
